public_comment.topic: Chair invites a member of the public, addressed as Glenn, to participate fully in the discussion.

A resident raised sustained objections to the municipal buildings plan: wants alternative options (including a status-quo repair option) presented to voters, wants the project tied explicitly to the earlier TAP study's recommendations, preferred in-person meetings and building tours over Zoom, questioned siting the ACE program with the school and suggested Turkey Hill might better accommodate it, and raised concerns about the Adult Activity Center's space needs and the future of Town Hall if offices move out.

passed (roll call: Brian, Dave, Tom, Greg/Michael Ray all aye)

budget_items.what_was_said: A member asked for a running total of what the town has spent across all the design iterations for this project; the chair declined to state an exact figure on the record but guessed it may be in the millions.

budget_items.topic: TC Pasios building reuse cost estimate (2021)
budget_items.what_was_said: The 2021 TC Pasios design committee expected to seek funding to reuse the TC Pasios building, but construction costs rose sharply within six months of that estimate.
A member recalled that code upgrades alone at TC Pasios (plumbing, seismic, electrical) were estimated at one figure, with roughly the same amount again needed just to put the building back together.
The committee noted it used ARPA funds to finalize the design and minimize additional cost to the Lunenburg taxpayer.
Members noted the project's construction cost rose substantially the last time the town waited, citing an increase over roughly six months.
The chair said his own calculations suggest the project shrinks in scope or grows in cost by a similar amount for every two years town meeting delays a vote.

budget_items.topic: Current plan cost and size vs. earlier proposal
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair contrasted the current, smaller-footprint plan and its cost against the earlier, larger proposal, noting price per square foot has roughly doubled in recent years.
The chair discussed the current project's cost per square foot compared to a hypothetical much higher figure some in town might prefer to spend to avoid siting ACE in the building.

budget_items.topic: Turkey Hill rehabilitation vs. replacement estimate
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident cited a recently released study comparing the cost to rehabilitate versus replace the Turkey Hill school.

budget_items.topic: Cost of including PAC in the project
budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted that including the public access channel (PAC) facility costs roughly as much as including the ACE program space.

The finance committee representative said the project would push the town slightly above its debt policy threshold for two years at the outset before coming back below it, in what he called the worst-case scenario, and that timing works well as other debt falls off.

decisions.decision: Bold the phrase about including any other town-owned building and property in the scope/charge slide, since that was the substantive change that broadened the committee's charge.
Replace a planned 'existing buildings' slide with an 'impact of delays' slide addressing working conditions, capital-plan effects, and cost of waiting.
Rename the presentation's 'agenda overview' slide to 'topics we will cover' to sound less formal.
Chair will send the draft slides to committee members tonight for feedback to him only, and check in with available members tomorrow morning before finalizing the presentation for town meeting.
If the article passes, hold open houses for the public to view the buildings before the ballot vote, and the chair will film a short video of current building conditions to show at the meeting.

minutes.headline: Committee finished its town-meeting presentation for the municipal buildings plan; the chair is leaving the board.
minutes.summary: The committee reviewed and revised, line by line, the draft slide presentation it will give at Saturday's annual town meeting on the municipal buildings project (new town hall/school offices, Brooks House reuse, and future Turkey Hill work), including how to frame project history, cost escalation, and the case for acting now versus delaying. It also gave a Brooks House parking update drawn from the library trustees and school committee, heard extended public objections to the plan from a resident, and approved prior minutes before adjourning; the outgoing chair, departing the select board, announced this was effectively his last meeting in that role.

what_happened.line: The committee finished editing, line by line, the slide presentation it will give voters at Saturday's town meeting on the municipal buildings plan.
It replaced a planned slide on existing buildings with one on the cost of delay, addressing working conditions and capital-plan effects.
The finance committee's representative said the project would push the town's debt slightly above its own debt-policy threshold for two years before falling back below it.
A resident objected at length, asking that a status-quo repair option be presented to voters and questioning where the ACE program should be sited.
The outgoing chair said this was effectively his last meeting on the committee, as he is also leaving the select board.

why_it_matters: Town meeting on Saturday will vote on the municipal buildings article -- new town hall/school offices, Brooks House reuse and future Turkey Hill work -- which this presentation is built to explain.
The debt-policy threshold discussion touches how the project would be financed and for how long it affects the town's borrowing capacity.
A resident's request for a status-quo alternative and questions about siting ACE went into the record without being resolved before the vote.
